title: Induction for Directors of Regulated Firms
summary: A ten-module induction giving new directors of regulated firms the grounding to discharge their duties, understand supervisory expectations and oversee the firm's risks.
intro: This training programme equips new and recently appointed directors of regulated firms to discharge their duties with confidence: understanding the regulatory system, the firm's risks and what supervisors expect of the board.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give new directors a practical, jargon-free grounding in their legal and regulatory responsibilities and in how a regulated firm is supervised, run and controlled. Participants leave able to see the firm the way a supervisor does, ask the right questions from their first board meeting and protect themselves through sound oversight.
sections.What It Covers: Directors' duties, the regulatory system and supervisory expectations of boards, fitness and propriety, senior manager accountability, business model and risk profile, capital and liquidity, conduct and consumer outcomes, financial crime, governance and committees, board information and challenge, and personal liability and protection.
Intended Audience: Newly appointed non-executive, independent and executive directors of regulated firms
Directors moving into financial services from other sectors, or into a new type of regulated firm
Senior managers preparing for board appointment or approval by the authority
Learning Objectives: Explain directors' legal duties and the regulatory responsibilities that sit on top of them
Describe how the regulatory system works and what supervisors expect of boards
Assess the firm's business model, risk profile and financial resilience
Oversee conduct, consumer outcomes and financial crime using structured board-level questions
Evaluate governance, committee arrangements and the quality of board information
Identify personal liability risks and the protections available, and agree a personal induction plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two- to three-day programme or as a series of induction sessions for individual directors or the whole board. Each module combines a short briefing with case studies and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and the director's experience.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Senior management or board experience is helpful. No prior experience of financial services regulation is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: Directors' Duties in a Regulated Firm
modules.summary: The legal duties every director owes, how regulation adds to them, and the distinct roles of the chair, executive and non-executive directors.
objectives: Explain the core fiduciary and statutory duties of directors
Distinguish the roles of chair, executive and non-executive directors
Recognise how regulatory obligations extend directors' responsibilities
syllabus: Duties of care, skill, diligence, loyalty and independent judgement
Collective board responsibility and individual accountability
Conflicts of interest and related-party matters
Group structures: duties to the firm versus the parent

modules.title: The Regulatory System and Supervisory Expectations of Boards
modules.summary: How financial regulation is structured, how the authority supervises firms, and what supervisors expect to see from the board in practice.
objectives: Explain the objectives and architecture of financial regulation
Describe how risk-based supervision works and how firms are categorised
Identify what supervisors expect of boards and how they assess them
syllabus: Regulatory objectives: stability, consumer protection and market integrity
International standard-setters: FSB, Basel Committee, IOSCO, IAIS and FATF
Risk-based supervision, supervisory engagement and board meetings with the authority
Supervisory tools: from information requests to enforcement

modules.title: Fitness and Propriety
modules.summary: The standards directors must meet on appointment and continuously thereafter, how the authority assesses them and what can lead to withdrawal of approval.
objectives: Explain the fitness and propriety criteria: competence, integrity and financial soundness
Describe the approval process and the authority's interview and assessment practice
Recognise the ongoing obligations to notify and maintain fitness
syllabus: Competence, capability, honesty, integrity and reputation
Time commitment, independence and conflicts
Applications, interviews and how the authority reaches its decision
Ongoing fitness, notifications and withdrawal of approval

modules.title: Senior Manager Accountability
modules.summary: How senior manager accountability regimes allocate individual responsibility, what reasonable steps mean in practice, and how this shapes the board's oversight role.
objectives: Explain the purpose and core features of senior manager accountability regimes
Evaluate statements of responsibilities and the firm's responsibilities map
Apply the reasonable steps standard to the director's own role
syllabus: Prescribed responsibilities, statements of responsibilities and mapping
Conduct rules and the duty of responsibility
Evidencing reasonable steps: delegation, oversight and records
Handovers and gaps in accountability

modules.title: The Firm's Business Model and Risk Profile
modules.summary: How to understand quickly what the firm does, how it makes money, where its key risks sit and how a supervisor would view its business model.
objectives: Analyse how the firm generates revenue and where its key dependencies lie
Identify the firm's principal risks and how they connect to its strategy
Assess the business model through a supervisor's eyes
syllabus: Business model, value chain and key dependencies
Principal risks and the risk management framework
Risk appetite: what the board has agreed and why
How supervisors assess business model viability and sustainability

modules.title: Prudential Basics: Capital and Liquidity
modules.summary: Plain-language grounding in why regulated firms must hold capital and liquidity, how requirements are set and what the board must monitor and approve.
objectives: Explain the purpose of capital and liquidity requirements
Interpret the firm's capital and liquidity position and its buffers
Recognise the board's role in internal assessments, stress testing and recovery planning
syllabus: Capital resources, requirements and buffers in plain language
Liquidity risk, funding and client money
Internal capital and liquidity assessments and board approval
Stress testing, recovery and wind-down planning

modules.title: Conduct and Consumer Outcomes
modules.summary: The board's responsibility for treating customers fairly, how poor outcomes arise and how the board gains assurance that products and services deliver good outcomes.
objectives: Explain conduct and consumer protection obligations and the shift to outcomes
Evaluate product governance, pricing, communications and support
Use conduct MI and complaints data to identify harm
syllabus: Fair treatment, suitability and consumer protection obligations
Product governance and value
Vulnerable customers and communications
Complaints, redress and conduct MI

modules.title: Financial Crime
modules.summary: The firm's exposure to money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions breaches, fraud and bribery, and the controls and reporting the board should expect.
objectives: Explain the main financial crime risks and the firm's legal obligations
Assess the firm's financial crime risk assessment and control framework
Oversee the MLRO's reporting and the resources given to financial crime compliance
syllabus: FATF standards and the risk-based approach
Customer due diligence, monitoring and suspicious activity reporting
Sanctions, fraud, bribery and corruption
The MLRO's annual report and board-level financial crime MI

modules.title: Governance, Committees and Board Information
modules.summary: How board and committee arrangements work in a regulated firm, how to read board packs critically and how to challenge management effectively.
objectives: Evaluate the firm's governance structure, committee mandates and reporting lines
Interpret board information and identify what is missing
Apply effective challenge techniques in the boardroom
syllabus: Board, risk, audit, remuneration and nomination committees
The three lines of defence and access to control function heads
Reading board packs: quality, timeliness and comfort without evidence
Constructive challenge, minutes and evidencing oversight

modules.title: Personal Liability, Protection and Induction Plan
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining personal liability, the protections available to directors and a practical plan for the director's first year on the board.
objectives: Identify the routes to personal regulatory, civil and criminal liability
Evaluate protections including indemnities, insurance and independent advice
Produce a personal induction and development plan
syllabus: Enforcement against individuals: case studies and lessons
Indemnities, directors' and officers' insurance and independent advice
Record-keeping, dissent and when to resign
Workshop: the director's first-year induction plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.
